response.summary: Draft r2 is well sourced. The redaction refusal that protects baseline keys has no criterion. RC-D5 contradicts the acceptance_ready invariant. evidence.observation: The plan defines the key as `(address, canonical JSON of the offending row)` and says an id-less constraint uses a positional address. response.summary: Reviewed the r2 plan bytes only, as this seat is instructed. Three blocking concerns: RC3-C4 asserts a violation-key stability under rule insertion that §2.3 and RC-D4 explicitly deny for positional addresses; RC4's 'payload records the option' has no named home while §3 declares RC4 independent of RC1, so the record can land in a variant rule 7 freezes; and the §5 claim that versions 3-14 keep their bytes has no criterion beyond the v7 rf1 goldens. Hardening concerns cover unnumbered time bounds resting on O15 (marked claim), the load-bearing redaction/temporal refusal that has no criterion and cites a nonexistent '(RC1 D3)', the unspecified --baseline x --allow-vacuous outcome although both phases edit band(), RC6 having neither budget nor resolved gate, RC1's gate having no recorded pre-change baseline against 24 failing tests, RC5-C2's 'one home' contradicting the §3 row that names two and omits the third spelling, the coverage.py move whose consumer tests are outside RC1's gate, and remedy being optional so existing rationale-only models still carry no author message. The obligations map covers O1-O17 and all five source requests, sequencing RC1->RC2->RC3 is sound, and O16/O17 are internally consistent; I could not open src/gnd/address.py, coverage.py or model_index.py to verify the cited line numbers because this seat reviews inline bytes only.

evidence.observation: RC3-C4: key survives inserting a rule above another and inserting a fact above another.

concerns.recommendation: The criterion unconditionally claims the baseline key survives rule and fact insertion. However, per RC-D4 and O10, constraints without an ID use positional addresses and version 15 offending rows use positional fact indices, both of which change under insertion and break the key. Restrict RC3-C4 to apply only to rules with declared IDs and redesign the baseline key to avoid using positional fact indices, or the RC3 contract is demonstrably broken.
concerns.title: Baseline key stability criterion contradicts positional addressing and fact indices

evidence.observation: The plan states: "Models with an active redaction policy or temporal terms re-project to versions 10/13 (`_project_result` in `src/gnd/checking_service.py`); `--rule-ids` refuses them in this milestone (RC1 D3)." The cited code does not match: `_project_result` sets `payload["schema_version"] = 11` for temporal models (src/gnd/checking_service.py:574), and `current_payload_schema_version` in src/gnd/payloads.py selects 9 for redaction-active plain checks, 11 for temporal, 7 otherwise; 10/13 appears only in the admission arm (`requested_check_schema_version`, payloads.py:749-767) and as the post-projection redaction wire (`payload["schema_version"] = 13 if ... == 13 else 10`, src/gnd/redaction.py:732). A refusal gate keyed to the stated {10,13} version set would miss temporal-model outputs, which land on version 11.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the citation to name all projected versions (9->10/13 redaction, 11 temporal) or, better, phrase RC1 D3's refusal in terms of model properties (active redaction policy, temporal terms) rather than wire versions, and pin the corrected fact in the RC1 spec.
concerns.title: Re-projection version claim in RC1 omits the temporal v11 arm

evidence.observation: RC2-C4 reads "time bound over 2,000+ edges" and RC3-C5 reads "time bound over 2,000+ rows". No numeric bound is stated anywhere in the plan, so a run of the stated work could not fail either criterion — any runtime satisfies it. Every other named criterion (e.g. RC1-C3 byte equality, RC3-C4 insertion stability) has a concrete falsifiable form; these two do not, despite the plan presenting them as named phase criteria and the rubric requiring falsifiability.

concerns.recommendation: Pin a numeric budget in each criterion (or explicitly defer the number to the spec with a requirement that the spec state one), e.g. derived from the O15 observation of 2.5 s for 2,047 edges, which the plan already records — marked as a claim, not reproduced.
concerns.title: Time-bound criteria are not falsifiable as written

evidence.observation: The table assigns the declared address to "`src/gnd/address.py` (`declared_constraint_address`, moved from `coverage.py`)". No `declared_constraint_address` exists in the repository: `src/gnd/address.py:49-52` already defines `constraint_address(constraint_id) -> "constraint:<id>"`, and `src/gnd/coverage.py:735-740` defines the separate positional-fallback helper `_constraint_address`. Nothing is "moved from coverage.py"; the declared form already lives in address.py. As written the plan risks creating a second name for an existing one-home function, contrary to binding rule 5 (one home).

concerns.recommendation: Reword the row to reuse the existing `constraint_address` in `src/gnd/address.py` (promoting it to the public effective view if needed) and keep `coverage._constraint_address` as the single fallback-aware caller, or state plainly that a new name is being introduced.
concerns.title: Declared-address artifact row misstates provenance and risks a duplicate home

evidence.observation: Completion predicate 1 claims "Version 7 bytes are unchanged for every existing input", but the only named byte-frozen criterion is RC1-C3: "without `--rule-ids`, output bytes for the rf1 sem-check goldens are unchanged", gated over "28 rf1 sem-check goldens" (§9). Nothing in the plan argues that those 28 files exercise every code path that emits version 7 (e.g. verify payloads, refusal paths, transition-adjacent arms also select v7 per src/gnd/checking_service.py:254,501,510,723), so the milestone could satisfy every stated criterion while the completion predicate's broader claim remains undemonstrated.

concerns.recommendation: Either narrow the completion predicate to the gated golden set, or name in the RC1/RC2 specs the additional v7-emitting paths (check, verify, refusal arms) whose outputs must also be byte-pinned.
concerns.title: v7-freeze gate is narrower than the completion predicate it backs

response.summary: Plan is well-grounded: reuse claims O16/O17 verified against src/gnd/address.py, src/gnd/coverage.py, src/gnd/model_index.py; O2/O3/O5/O6/O11/O13 verified against the cited schemas and checker code; sequencing RC1->RC2->RC3->RC6 with independent RC4/RC5 matches the dependency story; obligations map covers GR-D1, D2, D3, D5, D6 with observed-vs-claim discipline; version 15 is genuinely free in report.schema.json (legacy enum 3-11, wrapper consts 12/14). Four concerns: the 10/13 re-projection citation omits the temporal v11 arm, the two time-bound criteria are not falsifiable as written, the artifact table misstates the provenance of the declared-address helper, and the v7-byte-freeze gate covers fewer inputs than the completion predicate claims.

evidence.location: §2.4 lines 174-176 and RC4-C3 line 243, against rule 7 lines 95-97 and §2.3 line 162
evidence.observation: §2.4: "`--allow-vacuous` (run-wide) moves band 2 to 0 when vacuous verdicts are the only shortfall. Verdicts and counts are unchanged; the payload records that the option was used"; RC4-C3: "the payload records the option; vacuous verdicts still listed"; rule 7: "Version 7 and every other existing report variant keep their bytes." Unlike --baseline, which §2.3 says "(implies `--rule-ids`)", --allow-vacuous carries no such implication and is called run-wide. Context: src/gnd/payloads.py:169-234 builds the v7 payload as a fixed key set (schema_version, tool, command, outcome, exit_code, acceptance_ready, model, model_digest, population, counts, verdicts, derivations, coverage, extraction, issues, warnings, error, transition) with no options-bearing key, and the v7 branch of src/gnd/report.schema.json is additionalProperties:false, so on a plain `gnd check ... --allow-vacuous` run the option can be recorded only by adding a key that breaks the frozen closed shape.

concerns.recommendation: Name the recording home before the RC4 spec is approved: either state that --allow-vacuous implies --rule-ids and record the option only in version-15 payloads (as --baseline does), or scope RC4-C3's recording claim to version 15 and say what a frozen-variant run exposes (the changed exit code plus the still-listed vacuous verdicts).
concerns.title: RC4-C3 payload recording of --allow-vacuous contradicts binding rule 7 on plain (v7) runs

evidence.observation: RC3-C4: "key survives inserting a rule above another and inserting a fact above another", with no addressing precondition, while RC-D4 itself rules that a constraint without an id is keyed "by positional address, `addressing: positional` tells the caller it is unstable". Context: src/gnd/address.py:66-69 builds those refs as constraints[index] / fact_types[...].constraints[index], which shift exactly under the insertion the criterion tests.

concerns.recommendation: Scope RC3-C4 to declared-id addresses, or state the expected degradation for positional addresses (the key changes and is flagged by addressing: positional), so a test run of the stated work cannot fail the criterion in the case the plan itself declares unstable by design.
concerns.title: RC3-C4 key-stability criterion contradicts the plan's own positional-address ruling unless scoped to declared ids

response.summary: r2 verified against the cited code wherever it makes a checkable claim, and nearly all of it reproduces: the v7 verdict is closed with nine keys and no address (report.schema.json $defs/verdict); acyclic returns one cycle (checker/_core.py:1376-1378) while other ring variants list all offenders (1340-1375); band() sends vacuous to 2 (checker/_reports.py:146-168); the source enum has exactly the three spellings named (population.schema.json:18, population.py:131, extract/projection.py:278); the census addressing reused for address/addressing is real and spelled constraint:<id> with declared-id|positional (address.py:16,49; coverage.py:735; model_index.py:279); constraint_common has rationale and no remedy under unevaluatedProperties; version 15 is genuinely free (schema spans 3-11 via enum plus const 12, 13, 14; ReportSchemaVersion Literal ends at 13); _project_result re-projection exists (checking_service.py:520); the §9 gate files, the pyrel expected.json fixtures and the 28 sem-check goldens all exist; sequencing RC1->RC2->RC3->RC6 with RC4/RC5 independent is coherent, every obligation O1-O17 maps to a phase, every phase has line budgets and falsifiable criteria, and the claim-kind rows (O7-O9, O12, O14, O15) are honestly marked. One internal contradiction blocks the plan gate: RC4-C3 requires the payload to record --allow-vacuous use on a run-wide option that, unlike --baseline, is not stated to imply --rule-ids, while binding rule 7 freezes versions 3-14 byte-for-byte and the frozen v7 payload is a closed fixed key set (payloads.py:169-234; additionalProperties:false) with no key that could carry it — so as written RC4 cannot satisfy both its criterion and the freeze. Fix is one sentence; everything else stands.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. "No concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
Cite one concrete location in the plan for every concern.
Check that every phase criterion is falsifiable: a run of the stated work could fail it.

Check the frozen-variant claim: existing report versions (3-14) keep their bytes, and new meaning lands only in report version 15. Verify against src/gnd/report.schema.json and src/gnd/payloads.py where needed.
Check the baseline (RC3) contract: the violation key is stable under rule and fact insertion, and no run that failed to judge can yield a 'no new violations' claim.
Check sequencing and dependencies (RC1 -> RC2 -> RC3; RC4, RC5 independent) and that the obligations table maps every source request (issues GR-D1, D2, D3, D5, D6) to a phase.
Check the reuse claims (O16, O17) against the cited code: src/gnd/address.py, src/gnd/coverage.py, src/gnd/model_index.py.
Reject unbounded execution: each phase needs measurable budgets and a stop condition.
Flag any plan statement that relies on an unverified claim without saying so.
